paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: Isaiah sees a day when the dead places are glad. He says the wilderness and the dry land will be glad, and the desert will "rejoice and blossom like a rose" (Isaiah 35:1). And what do they see out there? "The glory of the LORD, the splendor of our God" (Isaiah 35:2). So if your life feels like dry ground right now, hold on to the picture Isaiah paints, because it ends in gladness.

And look who He's talking to. Isaiah says, "Strengthen the limp hands and steady the feeble knees!" (Isaiah 35:3). Then he tells anxious hearts, "Be strong, do not fear!" (Isaiah 35:4). God doesn't just fix the land. He comes "to save you" (Isaiah 35:4), and I think that's meant to land on tired people like you and me, so we can stand up and hold each other up.

Then comes the road. Isaiah says there will be a highway called the Way of Holiness, and "the redeemed will walk upon it" (Isaiah 35:8-9). They get there singing, "crowned with everlasting joy," while "sorrow and sighing will flee" (Isaiah 35:10). So hold on to this, baker: the ending belongs to the redeemed of the LORD, and it's JOY. That's what my ovens stay ready for.
